wall_set.local_finiteness: every compact interval meets A in finitely many points

completed_carrier.name: H_wall
completed_carrier.definition: f in L2(R), piecewise H1 on the components of R\A, with f'_reg in L2 and jump sequence ([f]_a) in ell2(A)
completed_carrier.dense_core: compactly supported functions that are H1 on finitely many wall intervals
completed_carrier.finite_cutoff_maps: restriction to the walls A_X is contractive and compatible under X<Y

closedness.proof_outline: a graph-Cauchy sequence converges in L2, its regular derivatives converge intervalwise, and its ell2 jump vectors converge; one-dimensional trace continuity on each locally finite interval identifies the limiting jumps
closedness.completeness: H_wall is the graph Hilbert space of D_wall

distributional_totalization.meaning: all regular-derivative and prime-wall contributions are retained by one closed countable graph

what_this_closes: common domain containing Evans histories and prime cut columns
source-metric adjoint for the history-plus-wall incidence
still_open: Fourier-Poisson action on the ell2 prime-wall jump coordinates
maximal-isotropic sewing for the completed history-plus-wall boundary relation
ordered linking skew form continuity on H_wall
adoption as the conservative C_FP history domain
disposition: The finite common history-plus-wall domains admit a canonical unweighted ell2 prime-wall completion. The differential is closed and the half-density prime incidence is Hilbert-Schmidt with the exact convergent sum over 1/(p log p). The next obstruction is sewing/linking structure, not analytic domain closure.
